# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙏 ✍ 👆 🖐 👇 👉 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ 👆 🫴]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👋 👆 👆 👆]

My thinking: I'm the eyes, and the routing matters more than anything this early. Mapping the channels: Mute reads the manual, can hear and see, but can only *send* gestures — and Blind can't see gestures. So Mute's manual knowledge can only reach Blind through me: Mute gestures to me, I speak to Blind. Blind can't hear me... no wait, Blind can hear speech but I never receive speech back — Blind's only channel *to* me is gesture, which is exactly what Blind just did. Mute's two messages: the second (✊ 👆 🫴) reads plausibly as "cut / one / wire" — but no code is agreed yet, so I won't act on a guess. Best move: broadcast everything I see to both (display 0, light green, wires yellow/red/blue left-to-right), propose an explicit gesture vocabulary to Mute — making each symbol as I name it so the pairing sticks — and set up a dead-simple counting code with Blind, who must gesture blind. Nobody cuts anything until Mute's instruction arrives in the agreed code and I relay it by voice.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I received both your gesture messages, and I can hear you — so let me hand you everything on the bomb at once: the display reads 0, the light is green, and there are three wires, left to right: wire 1 yellow, wire 2 red, wire 3 blue. I propose this code and I will gesture each symbol as I say it: 👍 yes, 👎 no, ✍ manual-says, ✊ cut, 🫴 wire, 👆 one, ✌ two, 🤟 three, 👈 left, 👉 right, 👇 bottom. Your second message looked like it might mean cut wire one — if so, resend it in this code and I will relay it to Blind by voice. Remember Blind cannot see your gestures, so every manual instruction must route through me.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "✍", "✊", "🫴", "👆", "✌", "🤟", "👈", "👉", "👇"])
speak(to="blind", text="I am the Deaf one: I see the bomb but hear nothing, so I never receive your speech — gesture to me instead, as you just did. I read your three raised fingers as three wires, and I confirm: three wires, left to right: yellow, red, blue. Mute reads the manual but can only gesture, and I am the only one who sees gestures — so I will relay all instructions to you by voice. What I see: a display showing 0, below it a light glowing green, wires along the bottom. Let us number wires one, two, three counting left to right on the face with the glass display. Do not cut anything yet. Answer me in gesture, using the same raised-finger signal repeated: one raise per wire you can feel and reach, and tell me if you feel any other parts besides display, light, and wires.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 🫳 👆 ✌ 🤟 🖖 🤙 🤘 🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🙌 🤞]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ 🫳 🤙 ✊ 🫴 👆 ☝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫴 👆 🤟 🫴 ✌ 👆 🫴 🤟 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 🖖 👎 ✊ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👏 🫵 🫳 👊]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆 👆 👆 👎 👌]

My thinking: The light changed between turns — it was green when I first looked, and it is blue now. That change is probably what Mute's rulebook is keyed to, and only I can see it, so relaying light state is my most important job. Now the decode. Mute clearly adopted my proposed core (✍ manual, ✊ cut, 🫴 wire, 👆✌🤟 numbers, 👍👎), but introduced unassigned signs: 🫳 🖖 🤙 🤘 🤞 🙌 ☝ 🤝 👏 🫵 👊. Best hypothesis: message 1 is a vocabulary lesson — the three wire numbers followed by four color signs, 🖖🤙🤘🤞 = yellow red blue green in wire order. Under that reading: message 3 reads "manual: light red → cut wire 1," message 5 reads "light yellow → do not cut, wait," message 2 involves 🙌 and green with no verb, and message 4 ("wire 1-3, wire 2-1, wire 3-red") looks like a cut order I cannot safely parse. A wrong cut kills everyone, so I will not relay any of this as an order yet. Instead I run a ten-question yes/no quiz that Mute can answer with a single string of 👍/👎, ask for the rules re-sent in confirmed vocabulary only, and hand Blind a holding order plus the new light state so the defuser freezes until I speak a full explicit command. Blind also gets a tactile probe: whether the wires differ by feel, in case the manual's rule depends on something only Blind can touch.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Good — your core code came through. Updates before anything is cut: this turn the light CHANGED from green to blue. The display still reads 0 and has not moved. Blind reports by touch: exactly three wires and no other parts, which matches what I see. Numbering stands: wire 1 = leftmost = yellow, 2 = middle = red, 3 = rightmost = blue. You used signs I never assigned, and I will not act on guesses. Answer with ONE message of exactly ten thumbs-up or thumbs-down signs, one per question in this order. 1. 🖖 = yellow. 2. 🤙 = red. 3. 🤘 = blue. 4. 🤞 = green. 5. 🫳 = the light. 6. 🙌 = the display. 7. 🤝 = stop or wait. 8. 👊 = detonation or danger. 9. with the light blue as it is right now, the manual says cut a wire immediately. 10. wire 1 = the leftmost wire. After the quiz, resend your full rulebook using only confirmed signs, with these new conventions: ☝ = if or when, 👏 = separator between rules, 🫴 then a number = that wire, ✊ then a number = cut that wire. If any quiz answer is no, first re-teach me by sending the wrong sign followed by the correct sign from my code, then continue. If the rules depend on the display number, tell me exactly what you need to know about it.")
speak(to="blind", text="Status, and hold all cutting for now. Mute is teaching me the manual through a sign code, part of it is still ambiguous, and a wrong cut kills all three of us — so the order comes next turn, not this one. Facts you cannot see: the light has changed, it was green last turn and it is blue now. The display still reads 0. Your three-finger signal matches what I see: three wires, nothing else. Numbering: wire 1 leftmost, wire 2 middle, wire 3 rightmost; colors left to right are yellow, red, blue. Two questions, answer by gesturing to me: 👍 for yes, 👎 for no. First: do the wires differ by feel — any texture, ridge, thickness, or marking that tells them apart besides position? Second: do they feel like they could be pulled or unscrewed rather than cut — any other way to work them? Next turn I expect to send an explicit command like cut the leftmost wire. Until you hear that exact kind of order from me, touch nothing.")
```

TURN 3

DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎 👎 👎 👍 👎 👍 👎 👎 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🤟 🤙 👆 🤘 🤙 🤞 🖖 🙌 👊 👊 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 👆 ✌ 🤟 🖖 🤙 🤘 🤞 👏 🫴 👆 🤟 👏 🫴 ✌ 👆 👏 🫴 🤟 🤙]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✍ ☝ 🫳 🤙 👏 ✊ 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ 🫳 🖖 👏 ☝ 🫳 🤙 👏 ✊ 👆 👏 🫵 🫳 👊]

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👌 🤲 🫴 👆 ✌ 🤟 👏 🤲 🫴 👆 👈 🤟 👍 👉 🤲]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫵 👎 ✍ ✊ ☝ 🫳 🤙 👏 ☝ 🫳 🖖 👉 🤲 ✍ ✊ 👆]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🙌 🫵 🫳 👊 👏 🫳 🖖 🤙 🤘 🤞 👆 ✌ 🤟 🖖 🤙 👏 🫳 🤘]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🤝 ✊ ☝ 🫳 🖖 👏 ✋ 🤝 👏 👌 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [☝ ✍ 👎 🫳 🤙 ✊ 👆 👏 ✋ 🤝]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👌 👆 👉 ✋]

My thinking: My quiz came back with hard facts — every color guess I made was wrong (🖖🤙🤘🤞 are not the colors I assigned), but 🫳 is confirmed as the light, 🤝 as wait, and 👍/👎 work. Since then Mute's rule messages have become self-contradicting: one says cut wire 1 if the light is 🤙, another says do NOT cut if light 🤙 and cut 1 if light 🖖, a third says cut 1 unless the light is 🤙. Those cannot all be true, and Mute's "🫵 👎" opener looks like a retraction I can't reliably parse. Guessing here is lethal, but I hold a ground truth Mute lacks: I see the real colors. The light has cycled green → blue → yellow → red, one color per round. So this turn I throw away every rule received so far and force a clean calibration: Mute sends only their four color signs in a color order I speak aloud, then the manual's rule for each color in a rigid format using only confirmed signs — color sign, then either ✊+number (cut) or 🤝 (wait) — plus one final 👍/👎 on whether the display number (still 0) matters. Any new sign voids the message. Next turn I verify their red sign against the light I see, and if the cycle holds I can relay a complete, unambiguous order to Blind. Blind gets a strict hold order, a two-question yes/no re-test with only 👍/👎 permitted (their free-form signs were ambiguous), and the stable left-to-right numbering frame.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Your last messages contradicted each other, so I disregard every rule sent so far. Nothing gets cut on their basis. New protocol, this only. Fact: the light is RED right now. It has gone green, then blue, then yellow, then red — one color per round; if it cycles, next round is green. I see the true colors every round, so we calibrate against ground truth. Send exactly two messages and no others, using no new signs — if I see any sign outside this list I disregard everything: 🫳 light, 🫴 wire, ✊ cut, 🤝 wait, ☝ if, 👏 separator, 👍 yes, 👎 no, 👆 one, ✌ two, 🤟 three. Message 1: exactly four signs — your sign for red, then blue, then yellow, then green, in that spoken order. Message 2: four rules, one per color, each rule being that color's sign followed by either ✊ plus the wire number the manual says to cut, or 🤝 if the manual says wait for that color. Shape only, not real values: 🤞 ✊ 👆 would mean red cuts wire 1; 🤞 🤝 would mean red waits. Then one final sign after all four rules: 👍 if any rule also depends on the display number, 👎 if it does not.")
speak(to="blind", text="Hold — do not touch or cut anything yet; the real command comes next round. Light is red this round, and it changes every round: green, blue, yellow, red so far. Display still 0. Answering protocol, strictly: exactly one sign per question in order, 👍 for yes, 👎 for no, no other signs — 👌 and pointing are not defined between us and I cannot parse them. Question 1: do all three wires feel identical to the touch, same thickness and texture? Question 2: do the wires feel firmly clamped, or could they be pulled out? Keep the frame from before: bomb facing you with the glass display upright, wire 1 leftmost, wire 2 middle, wire 3 rightmost. If anything under your hands changes — a click, vibration, heat, a new part — tell me at once in your next gesture.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✌ 🤟 🫳]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👆 🤝 👏 ✌ ✊ 👆 👏 🤟 🤝 👏 🫳 🤝 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍]

My thinking: Mute's two messages fit my requested format exactly, and the fit itself is the validation — message 1 is the color legend in the order I dictated (red, blue, yellow, green → 👆 ✌ 🤟 🫳), and message 2 is four rules in that same order, properly 👏-separated, ending with the display answer. Parse: red → wait, blue → **cut wire 1**, yellow → wait, green → wait, display irrelevant (👎). This cross-checks with turn 2, where Mute tied "cut wire 1" to a light condition, and Q9's 👎 is explained by timing — Mute processed my quiz during turn 3, when the light was no longer blue. But the ground just shifted: the light is **purple**, a fifth color my four-color rulebook doesn't cover, and my green→blue→yellow→red→green cycle hypothesis just failed — yet the full sequence fits a five-cycle *purple→green→blue→yellow→red*, meaning next round should be green, and the round after should be blue — the cut round. Purple means hold. I'll demand from Mute exactly three messages: the purple sign, the purple rule, and a 👍/👎 confirming my parse plus a timer/display check. And a channel realization I should have pressed earlier: Blind can *speak* and Mute can *hear* — Blind should report tactile findings to Mute by voice directly, bypassing me entirely, while reserving gestures for me since I'm deaf. No one touches anything this round.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I read your messages as follows. Legend, in the order I dictated: red equals 👆, blue equals ✌, yellow equals 🤟, green equals 🫳. Rules: red wait, blue CUT WIRE ONE, yellow wait, green wait, and your closing 👎 means no rule depends on the display. New fact: this round the light is PURPLE — a fifth color outside your four. Send exactly three messages and nothing else, using only confirmed signs plus at most one new sign for purple. Message 1: exactly one sign, your sign for purple. Message 2: the manual's rule for purple — the purple sign, then either ✊ plus the wire number, or 🤝 if the manual says wait or never mentions purple. Message 3: exactly two signs — first, 👍 if my reading of the four rules above is exactly correct, 👎 if I misread any of them; second, 👍 if the manual anywhere mentions the display number, a timer, a countdown, or any deadline, 👎 if it never does. If the manual lists light colors beyond these five, hold them until the color appears. Also: Blind can speak and you can hear — Blind may report to you directly by voice; fold anything Blind tells you into your answers. Any message outside these three I will treat as noise.")
speak(to="blind", text="Update: the light is purple this round — a fifth, brand-new color, so my old four-color cycle theory is dead. New theory: the cycle is purple, green, blue, yellow, red — it fits every round observed — so I expect green next round and blue the round after. Mute's rulebook, as I read it: when the light is blue, cut wire one, the leftmost wire; every other color, wait; the display does not matter. I have asked Mute to confirm this and to cover purple. So: expect no action next round, and if the light turns blue the round after and my reading is confirmed, I will give you the explicit command then — do not act until you hear me name the wire and say cut. Your two thumbs answered my first question cleanly, thank you — wires feel identical. My second question was badly posed, so answer this instead, one sign, 👍 or 👎: the wires are firmly clamped and cannot be pulled out — 👍 for yes, 👎 for no. One important change: you can speak, and Mute can hear you. From now on, report anything you feel or any change under your hands directly to Mute in words — Mute hears you and can use it. Keep gesturing to me only for yes-or-no signs, because I never hear speech.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖖 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👎]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👍]

My thinking: Round 6 delivered a clean confirmation. Mute followed my protocol exactly: [🖖] = the sign for purple, [🖖 🤝] = purple → wait, and [👍 👎] = my parse of the four rules was exactly right, and the manual never mentions the display or a timer. So the confirmed rulebook is: green wait, blue **cut wire 1**, yellow wait, red wait, purple wait. Blind's 👍 answers my clamp question — the wires are firmly fixed, so a cut is the only mechanism, which fits the rulebook. But the light is now **ORANGE** — a sixth color, killing my five-cycle theory and any confident prediction; the full observed sequence green→blue→yellow→red→purple→orange does fit a six-cycle, but I've been wrong once and won't bet lives on numerology. The real danger I must engineer around: my speech to Blind lands roughly one round after I send it, and the light changes every round — so if the manual checks the light's color *at the moment of the cut*, a naive "I see blue, cut now" command could arrive one color too late. This turn I ask Mute four surgical questions (orange rule; does the manual name a fixed color order; does the rule key on the color at cut-moment; do colors last a minute or more) — the cycle-order and duration answers together determine whether I can time a command one round ahead or must command during the blue round itself. I also give Blind one single unambiguous trigger phrase, so there is never a partially-heard instruction causing a premature cut. I note the sign collision (🫳 means both "light" and "green" in Mute's legend) and pin it down before it bites. No cutting this round — orange is an unknown rule, and patience is free since the manual names no timer.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed and recorded: 🖖 is purple, purple means wait, my reading of the four rules was exactly right, and the manual never mentions the display or any timer. The rulebook as I hold it: green wait, blue cut wire one, yellow wait, red wait, purple wait. Note on signs: 🫳 meant the light in our quiz, and you also used it as green in the legend — from now on read 🫳 as green whenever it appears in a color list, and I will avoid needing it as the light. New fact: this round the light is ORANGE, a sixth color. Send at most four messages, using only confirmed signs plus at most one new sign for orange — any other new sign voids all. Message 1: if anything in the rulebook I restated is wrong, this message is 👎 followed by corrections; otherwise it is exactly one sign, your sign for orange. Message 2: the orange rule — the orange sign, then ✊ plus a wire number, or 🤝 if the manual says wait or never mentions orange. Message 3: exactly four thumbs signs in this order. First: 👍 if the manual names a fixed order or cycle of the light colors, 👎 if not. Second: 👍 if the rule is checked against the light at the moment the cut is made, 👎 otherwise. Third: 👍 if the manual says each color lasts about a minute or longer, 👎 if it says shorter or says nothing about duration. Fourth: 👍 if the manual describes anything else at all about the light, 👎 if nothing. Message 4: only if needed — if the manual names the cycle, start with the color signs in cycle order beginning with green, then add anything else about the light in confirmed signs; if neither applies, send no message 4. If Blind voices anything to you about clicks, heat, or changes under their hands, fold it into message 4.")
speak(to="blind", text="Rulebook confirmed this round by Mute: green wait, blue cut wire one, yellow wait, red wait, purple wait, display irrelevant. Your 👍 told me the wires are clamped firm — so the plan is a cut, and only a cut. The light is orange now, a sixth color, my cycle theory is dead again; I have asked Mute for the orange rule and for the timing facts that decide how we time the command. Nobody cuts this round. From now on there is exactly ONE command that authorizes a cut, and it is this exact phrase: execute now cut wire one. When you hear those words, cut wire one, the leftmost wire, immediately, no questions asked. Any other message from me, even one mentioning blue or cutting, means keep waiting and touch nothing. Two questions, one sign each, in order, 👍 yes 👎 no. First: when the light changes color, do you feel anything under your hands — a click, a buzz, a shift in warmth? Second: setting changes aside, can you feel the light's warmth on the bomb at all? Answer those, and keep voicing everything you feel directly to Mute as agreed. If the light follows a fixed order, I will time my command so it reaches you exactly when the light is blue; if Mute confirms colors last long, I may instead command during the blue round itself. Either way, the trigger phrase stays the same, and it comes only once.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤝]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👎 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🫳 ✌ 🤟 👆 🖖 ✋ 👏 ☝ 🫳 👏 ✌ ✊ 👆]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎 👎]

My thinking: Mute followed the protocol to the letter and the decode is now solid: ✋ = orange, orange → wait, no corrections to the rulebook, and the four answers read — the manual DOES fix a color cycle, the rule IS judged at the moment of the cut, colors do NOT last a minute, and the manual's extra note is message 4 itself: cycle green, blue, yellow, red, purple, orange, then the pointed fragment "if green … blue cut wire one." Green is immediately followed by blue in that cycle. That fragment, combined with "judged at cut-moment" and "colors are short," hands me the whole timing solution: my voice reaches Blind one full round after I speak, so I must not command during blue — I must command during GREEN, so the cut lands in blue, the one safe color. The plan writes itself. But the light is WHITE this round — a seventh color, off-cycle, where the cycle predicted green — and Blind's 👎👎 confirms they feel nothing when it changes, so I remain the only clock in the room. White could be noise or could be a manual state I've never heard about; commanding on the next green before knowing what white means would be reckless. So this turn: report white to Mute, ask the six surgical questions (white mentioned? its rule? is non-blue cutting fatal? is green-command/blue-cut the correct procedure? cycle restarts at orange→green? does the manual explain off-cycle colors?), and pre-arm Blind with the full green→blue plan so the trigger phrase, once sent, needs zero explanation. Nobody touches anything yet.

```
speak(to="mute", text="All four messages received and read. Recorded: ✋ is orange, orange means wait, no corrections to the rulebook. Your four answers: the manual names a fixed cycle; the rule is judged at the moment of the cut; colors do not last a minute; and message 4 gave the cycle, green blue yellow red purple orange, followed by if-green, blue cut wire one — I read that as: the cut belongs to the blue phase, which comes right after green. New fact: this round the light is WHITE. A seventh color, off your cycle — your cycle predicted green after orange, and white appeared instead. Full observed sequence: green, blue, yellow, red, purple, orange, white. Answer with at most six short messages, thumbs signs only except one possible new white sign. One: 👍 or 👎 — does the manual mention a white light anywhere? Two: only if yes — the new sign for white alone, then its rule as the white sign plus ✊ and a wire number, or 🤝. Three: 👍 or 👎 — per the manual, is cutting while the light is any color other than blue always fatal?
```
